name: Faselane AI
tagline: An AI assistant product that runs prompt-driven workflows over your own text and documents.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The public footprint here is thin, so treat this entry as a category verdict rather than a forensic teardown. Products in this shape are usually a hosted UI over someone else's model: prompt templates, a step runner, a history of past outputs. That shell is genuinely a one-sitting build, and the model you would call is the same model they call. Where it stops being trivial is everything around the shell: connectors to Drive or Slack or your CRM, OAuth for each of them, reliable background execution, and prompt chains that someone already spent months tuning so they do not fall over on messy input. Build it if your workflows are yours and few; pay if you need it to touch six other systems.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you define multi-step prompt workflows with variables, run them against pasted text or uploaded documents, and keep a searchable history of every run.
requirements: An OpenAI-compatible API key, billed to you per token
Somewhere to run localhost, or a small VPS if you want it away from your laptop
whatYouLose: Prebuilt integrations and the OAuth plumbing behind them, which is where most of the real work hides
Prompt chains that someone else already tuned against thousands of ugly real inputs
Mobile access, unless you host it and bolt on a login
Someone to blame when the model provider has an outage or silently changes behavior
Team sharing, permissions, and a shared library of workflows
moatNotes: No data moat visible, and the model is rented. The defensible part is the connectors and the tuning, not the idea.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the interesting part of an AI workflow tool is not the prompt box, it is the fifty small decisions about chunking, retries, file parsing, and what to do when the model returns something malformed. A paid product has already eaten those decisions, plus it already talks to the systems your work lives in. If your use case is three prompts you run on text you paste in yourself, you are paying rent on a wrapper. If it is pulling from four SaaS tools on a schedule and handing results to colleagues, the subscription is cheaper than your weekend.
notes: Filed on a thin public record, so the verdict describes the category more than the specific product.
prompt:
Build a local-first AI workflow runner. Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, one file at ./data/app.db
- Any OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, base URL and API key read from .env.local

In scope:
1. Workflows: name, description, and an ordered list of steps. Each step holds a prompt template with {{variable}} placeholders, an optional model override, and an optional temperature.
2. Inputs: a run form that auto-generates fields for every variable used in the workflow, plus a text area for pasted content and an upload box for .txt, .md, and .pdf files. Extract plain text from PDFs, no OCR.
3. Execution: run steps in order, streaming each step's output to the page as it arrives. The previous step's output is always available to the next as {{previous}}. If a step fails, stop and show the raw error.
4. Runs: persist every run with its inputs, per-step outputs, model used, token counts, and wall-clock duration.
5. Library: list past runs, filter by workflow, full-text search over outputs.
6. Export: download any run as a single markdown file.
7. Seed the database with three example workflows: summarize and extract action items, rewrite for a specific audience, and turn messy notes into a structured brief.

Out of scope, do not build any of it:
- Auth, users, roles, billing, telemetry, analytics
- Cloud deploy configs, Docker, queues, cron
- Third-party connectors, browser extension, mobile app
- Vector search or embeddings, keep it keyword search

Rules:
- Secrets only in .env.local, and ship a .env.example listing every key
- No network calls except the model endpoint
- Handle long inputs by truncating with a visible warning rather than silently dropping text
- npm install then npm run dev must work with no manual database setup
- Write a README with setup in under ten lines and a short note on how to add a workflow
